State law requires every motor vehicle operator and every owner to carry some form of liability insurance, and the guide calls that requirement Financial Responsibility. Notice that the rule reaches both groups: the person who drives and the person who owns the vehicle. We will look at what liability insurance pays for, when owners have to prove they carry it, which documents count as proof, and why that proof has to stay in the vehicle. By the end you should be able to name the accepted forms of proof and explain who can ask to see them.","fact_ids":["sec15-F01","sec15-F02","sec15-F04","sec15-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec15-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What liability insurance covers","fact_ids":["sec15-F02","sec15-R06","sec15-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Covers your legal liability to others.","fact_ids":["sec15-F02","sec15-R06","sec15-F01"]},{"text":"Others injured, or their property damaged.","fact_ids":["sec15-F02","sec15-R06","sec15-F01"]},{"text":"Most drivers buy from a company or agent.","fact_ids":["sec15-F02","sec15-R06","sec15-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Start with what the coverage does. Liability insurance covers the policyholder's legal liability when other people are injured or when their property is damaged. In plain terms, it answers for harm to other people and to their property. That is the coverage the state makes mandatory for every operator and owner under the Financial Responsibility rule. There are several ways to meet that rule, and the next lesson covers self-insurance, bonds and cash deposits. Most drivers, though, simply get their liability insurance from an insurance company or an agent rather than through self-insurance, bonds or cash, so a policy from a company or agent is the usual path.","fact_ids":["sec15-F02","sec15-R06","sec15-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec15-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Proof at registration","fact_ids":["sec15-F03","sec15-F13","sec15-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Show proof to register a vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec15-F03","sec15-F13","sec15-F01"]},{"text":"Show proof again to renew plates.","fact_ids":["sec15-F03","sec15-F13","sec15-F01"]},{"text":"Sign a form promising to stay insured.","fact_ids":["sec15-F03","sec15-F13","sec15-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Owners prove their coverage at two moments. Vehicle owners must show proof of insurance when they register a vehicle, and they must show it again when they renew their plates. Registration also comes with a promise in writing. When you register a vehicle, you sign a form saying that you have insurance and that you will keep it on the vehicle. So the paperwork does two jobs: the proof shows that you are insured right now, and the signed form commits you to keeping that insurance on the vehicle afterward. Registration and plate renewal are the checkpoints where an owner shows the coverage that the Financial Responsibility rule requires.","fact_ids":["sec15-F03","sec15-F13","sec15-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec15-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Accepted forms of proof","fact_ids":["sec15-F04","sec15-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Current insurance ID card, policy, or binder.","fact_ids":["sec15-F04","sec15-F05"]},{"text":"Paid receipt showing the policy.","fact_ids":["sec15-F04","sec15-F05"]},{"text":"Department self-insurance certificate or bond ID card.","fact_ids":["sec15-F04","sec15-F05"]},{"text":"Proof on a handheld electronic device.","fact_ids":["sec15-F04","sec15-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Now the list of what counts as proof. Second, a binder is a temporary insurance policy, and it appears right beside the policy itself on the list. The self-insurance certificate and the bond ID card belong to owners who use the other Financial Responsibility options, which the next lesson explains. The fifty thousand dollar figure is the total for everyone injured in that crash, and each individual's minimum remains twenty-five thousand dollars.
